definition: In artificial intelligence (AI), anticipation occurs when an agent makes decisions based on its explicit beliefs about the future.
details: More broadly, "anticipation" can also refer to the ability to act in appropriate ways that take future events into account, without necessarily explicitly possessing a model of the future events. The concept stays in contrast to the reactive paradigm, which is not able to predict future system states.
story: Imagine handing a to-do list to a very clever intern who refuses to guess: before each step, they look around, check the result, and adjust. It is the difference between a search engine and a helper who actually finishes the task. The machine stops just answering one question and starts getting a job done, step by step, checking its work along the way. It is a loop of look, act, and learn — the same way you cook from a recipe you have never tried: add, taste, correct. And that habit of checking, acting, then checking again is Anticipation (artificial intelligence).
